plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and build cash.
Increase QQQI to 25% for income and stability.

conservative.read: This plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces leverage and single-stock concentration, holding a larger cash buffer for stability and lower drawdowns.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to minimal levels.
Maintain small positions in MUU and METU.
Trim SPY to 25% to balance index exposure and cash.
Reduce CRWD to 10% to manage concentration.
Add GEV as a new high-quality position.
This plan balances risk reduction with selective growth opportunities.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets ~2.5% monthly return by reducing leverage and concentration while adding a promising new name. It aims for risk-first growth, maintaining a moderate cash buffer and keeping overall leverage in check.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to free up capital for higher-conviction trades.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs: SOXL to 7%, MUU to 6%, METU to 6%, SPAL to 6%.
Add GEV and TSM as new, high-scoring long setups.
This plan aggressively leans into leverage and concentration.
It aims for higher growth but accepts significantly increased drawdown risk.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% monthly return by maximizing leverage and concentrating on high-scoring setups, including leveraged ETFs. It accepts substantially higher potential drawdowns and the risks of leverage decay. Strict stop discipline is paramount.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) and volatile single names (CRWD, SNOW).
Trim SPY to 20% to increase cash and reduce concentration.
Increase QQQI to 30% to maximize income-generating assets.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions over growth.
It aims for low drawdowns and reliable income generation.
Distributions are variable and NAV can still decline in market selloffs.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets ~1% monthly return through distributions, prioritizing capital preservation and steady cash flow. It eliminates leverage and high-beta names, focusing on income ETFs and broad indices, while maintaining a cash buffer.
